match.reason: None of the bank points covers circle geometry: the alternate segment theorem and the tangent-secant result are about angles and lengths in a circle, whereas the bank points only cover derivatives, tangent lines and normals on curves.

draft.title: Alternate segment theorem and secants
card: The angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment. That is the angle at the circumference on the other side of the chord.
A tangent at \(A\) and a chord \(AB\) make an angle of \(40^{\circ}\). Any angle at the circumference standing on chord \(AB\), in the opposite segment, is also \(40^{\circ}\).
A secant is a line that cuts the circle at two points. A tangent from the same outside point touches the circle at one point.
The square of the tangent length equals the whole secant times its part outside the circle. Example: tangent 6, outside part 4, whole secant \(x\). Then \(6^{2} = 4 \times x\), so \(x = 9\).
draft.remember: The tangent-chord angle equals the angle in the alternate segment. Tangent squared equals whole secant times outside part.

a.q: A tangent from point \(P\) is 12 cm long. A secant from \(P\) has an outside part of 8 cm. What is the whole secant length?
a.why: Tangent squared equals whole secant times outside part, so \(12^{2} = 8 \times x\). That gives \(144 = 8x\) and \(x = 18\). Using 1.5 comes from dividing 12 by 8, which skips the squaring.
a.clue: Square the tangent first, then divide by the outside part.

b.q: A tangent at \(T\) meets chord \(TS\) at an angle of \(55^{\circ}\). Point \(R\) is on the circle in the alternate segment. What is \(\angle TRS\)?
b.why: The angle in the alternate segment equals the angle between the tangent and the chord, so \(\angle TRS = 55^{\circ}\). Doubling to \(110^{\circ}\) treats it as an angle at the centre, which is a different theorem.
b.clue: Match the angle between tangent and chord with the angle on the other side of the chord.

wants.brief: A circle with a tangent touching at point A and a chord AB. Mark the angle between the tangent and chord AB as 40 degrees. Mark point C on the circle in the opposite segment from that angle, and the angle ACB, also labelled 40 degrees.
wants.why: It shows which angle is in the alternate segment.

wants.brief: A circle with outside point P. A tangent PT of length 6 touches the circle at T. A secant from P crosses the circle at X, nearer, then Y. PX is labelled 4 and the whole secant PY is labelled x.
wants.why: It shows the tangent, the outside part and the whole secant.
